question: The first census of Independent India was conducted in 1951, which was the ____________ census in its continuous series.
solution:
The correct answer is __**eighth**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The census is a regular and systematic collection of data about the population.
 
• India has a long tradition of conducting the census, which started in 1872.
 
• The 1881 Census is considered the first complete census in India, marking the start of the continuous decennial census series under British colonial administration.
 
• The first census after India gained independence was conducted in 1951.
 
• This 1951 census was the eighth census in the continuous series that started in 1881.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census:**

 
 
• A census is the procedure of systematically acquiring and recording information about the members of a given population.
 
• It is a regular practice in many countries and typically takes place every 10 years.
 
• The data collected during a census can include information on various demographic, social, and economic characteristics.
 
• This data is crucial for planning and policy-making purposes.
 
 
 
• **History of Census in India:**
 
 
• The first complete census was taken in 1881, and since then, censuses have been undertaken uninterruptedly once every ten years.
 
• The census operations are organized under the Census Act of 1948.
 
• The responsibility for conducting the census lies with the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• The census data serves as a critical input for various government schemes and programs.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Census:**
 
 
• The census provides a snapshot of the population's size, distribution, and demographic characteristics.
 
• It helps in the allocation of government resources and representation in legislative bodies.
 
• The data aids in the planning and implementation of public policies and services such as healthcare, education, and transportation.
 
• The census also assists businesses in market research and strategic planning.
 
 
 
• **1951 Census:**
 
 
• The 1951 Census was the first census conducted after India gained independence.
 
• It marked the beginning of a new era in the collection of demographic data in India.
 
• The census provided valuable information about the population, including details on migration, literacy rates, and employment.
 
• This data was crucial for the country's planning and development initiatives during the early years of independence.
